source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The only published specification for Microsoft's Fulton County campus is 489,370 square feet of technical space, with no megawatt figure disclosed.

That absence is the pattern worth registering. Square footage describes a building, not a load. It cannot tell a reader whether the site is a training campus or a colocation hall, and those two have very different relationships to the grid. Any capacity number attached to this site by anyone else is an estimate, not a disclosure.

The state context makes the gap concrete. Georgia has 49 mapped facilities, and only 5 of them publish a megawatt figure. The published total across those 5 is 76.3 MW. This campus ranks sixth by published megawatt in the state, a ranking that exists in the state table but cannot be reconciled with the campus page, because the campus page publishes no megawatt figure at all. The distance between 49 mapped facilities and 5 with published power is the real story: Georgia's AI footprint is mostly unmetered in public, and this campus sits inside that unmetered majority even as it appears on a list built from the minority that does publish.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. There is no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power or cooling detail. No rack estimate can be derived from what is here, because square footage converts to capacity only through a density assumption the operator has not stated. The site sits 5.1 miles from Hartsfield Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is a location fact and not a capacity one.
